I have posted this idea numerous times on both Voat and Reddit to lackluster response, mostly criticism. However, now that some of the most respected names in Science have announced a Similar idea I would like to revisit my idea and see what Voat thinks.

**Sending Humans to the Alpha Centauri System **

Phase 1: Solar Powered Ultra High Powered Space Based Laser Array

Using current technology Space Based lasers can relatively easily be built in the 1-2 Petawatt range. Japan has already fired a 2 Petawatt laser here on Earth. A space based Petawatt laser would not need the massive cooling systems as an Earth based laser. Place one laser in Earth Orbit (High Earth Orbit), place a second laser on the backside of the moon and a third in Deep Space (an equal distance past the moon that the moon is from Earth).

Phase 2: Long Voyage Space Craft

Using current (and near future) technology build a Space ship roughly the size of the ISS (but more compact). Think DS9, Babylon 5 or one of the other myriad of Sci-Fi ships with a rotational component that simulated (created artificial) gravity. The ship would be built in Low Earth Orbit and then be boosted into space (past the first laser) using conventional rocket engines that detach once the ship is free of Earth's gravity. The ship would have:

* A crew of 10-20 people * Enough Plants, Fruit and Vegetable growing to both feed the crew and remove the CO2 from the air * Enough water on board for a 40 year trip and would recycle and purify Urine (think Bill Gate's purifier) to water the plants and trees * A plethora of Starshot sized Optical Probes that could be deployed enroute to relay (and amplify) signals from the ship to Earth and vice-versa * A reserved of Conventional Rocket Fuel (like would be used by Spaceship 2) for braking and maneuvering the ship once in the Alpha Centauri system as well as to fly reconnaissance missions using a shuttle craft (like Spaceship 2). * Multiple Solar Powered Lasers like what are in our system that they can drop in the Alpha Centauri system for a return voyage. They drop one as they enter the system, a second near the middle of the system and the third on a moon of a potentially habitable (needs further exploration) planet. * An absolutely massive Solar Array that can be deployed (and retracted if need be) that will be hit with the Lasers to propel the ship along it's journey. It would also provide enough power to power the ship for the first and last quarters of the trip. The middle half of the trip the ship would need to be powered by some kind of small fission/fusion reactor. Think small space cooled Nuclear Reactor. * Redundant CO2 scrubbers incase for some reason the Plant life is not sufficient in cleaning the CO2. * Front, rear and side directional liquid fuel thrusters for controlling the trajectory in voyage and for maneuvering the ship one each end of the voyage. * Sensor hub on the front of the ship capable of scanning for any dangers along the trip so course corrections can be made if need be. * Shuttle craft with every scanning and detection technology humanity possesses as well as HiDef audio and video recording functionality so that objects (Planets, moons, etc) in the Alpha Centauri system can be scanned and studied before humanity lands on those objects. * Redundant food stores (think MRE's) in case the food grown on board is not sufficient to feed the crew. * Redundant shuttle in case something happens to the primary shuttle or the main ship and the crew is forced to abandon ship. * An assortment of portable science and manufacturing equipment in case the crew does have to abandon ship and stay on one of the objects in the Alpha Centauri System. * Portable Emergency Habitat (think about the Concrete habs developed for a possible Mars settlement) that can be pre-loaded on both Shuttles and deployed by the crew on a Planet if needed. * The ability to manufacture fuel for the shuttles on planet if the crew has to stay on a planet. That way they can continue to survey the planet, mine, etc. while waiting for Rescue or future human settlers.

Phase 3: Launch of Ship

The first voyage to Alpha Centauri should be a carefully selected group of geeks, nerds and others with anti-social personalities. People with no real connection to anyone they would be leaving behind. Once the first ship is launched a second ship should begin construction to launch (in Emergency if needed) 10 years after the first ship. With the information and knowledge gathered from the first ship and it's crew the second ship could be massively larger and have a more diverse group of scientists, engineers, biologists, etc.

Phase 4: Launch second Ship

Ten years after the first smaller ship is launched a second ship with a crew of 10,000 people is launched. This will require previous deployment of additional lasers in the array as the ship will be so much larger it will take far more lasers to propel to a descent speed.

Summary:

By using a 1+ Petawatt laser array (3 lasers) the first smaller ship could easily reach speeds of .5C (half the speed of light) which would make the trip to Alpha Centauri only take a little over 2 years (Earth time). The trip for the crew would seem like only a few months. The crew could spend 1 year scouting and surveying the Alpha Centauri System before launching on their return trip to Earth. Total round trip would be 5 Earth years and to the crew would seem like about 3 years.

The second (and massively larger ship) would require 20-30 1+ Petawatt lasers in the array. At least 5 in High Earth Orbit, 5 on the back side of the moon, and a series of them across our solar system. It would take about 3 months to get the larger ship up to .5C but it would still be able to make the trip to the Alpha Centauri System in under 3 years Earth time. This ship would contain everything the crew would need to build a Permanent City on a planet in the Alpha Centauri System. Once the permanent settlement is built the crew could load the now empty cargo holds with Planet and Animal specimens, rock and mineral specimens and food and water and the ship could return to Earth with a skeleton crew (5-10 people) and be reused to send future Settlers and Supplies to Alpha Centauri.

My Personal Thoughts:

I don't think it is a matter of can we do it, or should we do it; but rather a matter of we have to do it. If for no other reason that to ensure the survival of the human race. The chances of finding new life, new cures for diseases, new and fascinating plant and animal life, new planets we can settle on and inhabit is too great to resist. Additionally, we could then use the Alpha Centauri system and a Solar Laser Array to reach other Star Systems even farther away. Who knows one of them may contain intelligent life, but we will never know unless we try.

The total cost for both ships, the laser arrays and all the equipment, supplies, etc. would be between 1-5 trillion depending on the number of countries and businesses that signed on to the project. The more people working on it the lower the costs would end up being.

I believe that humanity working together could launch the first ship in under 5 years if we set our minds to it....that means by 2025 would could have humans exploring Alpha Centauri and by 2030 have a permanent settlement in the Alpha Centauri System.

This can be achieved with most of our lifetimes and maybe even bring about the discovery of medicines and technologies to drastically lengthen and better our lives.

Actually it would need bigger and more complex cooling systems. Space is cold, yes, but because there is no atmosphere to conduct or convect heat away cooling something in space is difficult. Radiant cooling is much slower than conductive or convective cooling. Consider a vacuum thermos which keeps liquids hot or cold for hours longer than conventionally insulated bottles.

Cooling on Earth is easy by comparison because we have a sea of air we can move past our cooling fins and dump heat into.

To the Most Esteemed Chair of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System Janet Yellen,

I am writing you on the behalf of the manager of the sovereign fund of Luxembourg, but also to some minor extent, [worries shared in some of our private correspondences](https://voat.co/v/ModernPowers/comments/982312) ([M] link for context reference, not in game. [/M]). Although the Luxembourg government has helped in the process of recent liquidation of American sovereign capital, we are not sure whether this action can be sustained, and analysts at our central banks have been worried by several trends within the U.S. economy. This gives us pause whether to reverse our current actions. These concerns are as follows:

- [The U.S. deficit per annum remains one of the largest in the world](http://www.usgovernmentspending.com/federal_deficit_chart.html)

- [The debt has surpassed U.S. GDP](http://www.usdebtclock.org/).

- [Given current unfunded liabilities](http://archive.is/0Chie), these previous two bullet points do not seem to be trends that will continue downwards in the near future.

And, most importantly to our bottom line and financial position:

- [The real interest rate of most treasury products remain negative](https://www.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/Pages/TextView.aspx?data=realyield)

The first three suggest that the FED will be under severe pressure to continue to ease interest rates and inflate heavily in the future. This, and the last item alone suggests that unless some effort at reducing monetary inflation or pushing up nominal interest rate fixes by the Federal Reserve is done, but ideally other fiscally prudent measures, then the Luxembourg government would be forced to liquidate U.S. assets at least into some form of forex reserves, if not other capital assets.

We bring this up in order to ease some of the fear of my colleagues in the Central Bank, and to possibly address some of these concerns.

Sincerely,

Luc Frieden
